import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

The failure occurs after validation, store selection, and archival, specifically while writing the newly created epic bead ID back into the approved plan. I’m tracing that commit path and checking the archived plan’s repository state; because the plan is in the sidecar repository, the project instructions require me to open it through `/sase_repo` before inspecting it.

The rollback history exposes an important clue: the “restore” commit added the plan as a brand-new tracked file. That means the archived plan already existed only as an untracked worktree file, and the forward `bead_id` commit reported a no-op before rollback committed the restored copy. I’m now inspecting the exact workspace-0 clone used by the failed command and the store’s concurrent commit/push behavior to determine why Git saw no forward change.

The root cause is now concrete: while `sase-a7`’s 10 phases and 16 edges were being created, the launcher had already written `bead_id: sase-a7` into the plan but had not committed it. At 15:17:51, machine-managed repository recovery correctly acquired the SDD write lock, snapshotted that dirty file into recovery ref `c02bdd7c`, and hard-reset the clone to `origin/main`. Because the plan write itself held no SDD lock, recovery was allowed to erase it; when DAG creation finished, the targeted commit found no change and returned false.

This is a focused transactional bug with one implementation path and one regression suite, so I’m choosing a `tale` plan. The plan will make plan-content replacement and its Git commit one lock-protected operation, cover forward-link and rollback writes, verify the real recovery race, install the fixed build, and retry the exact epic command.

The required first `--explain` pass rejected the minimal frontmatter because the current validator requires `title` and `goal` alongside `tier`. I’m applying exactly those schema-required fields, then I’ll revalidate without `--explain` as instructed.

The tale plan now passes validation with zero warnings. I’m submitting it through `sase plan propose`; per `/sase_plan`, this hands control to the approval gate before any implementation files are changed.
